stories.title: RBI warns of inflation risks from West Asia conflict and El Nino, says economy remains resilient
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India highlighted that the ongoing conflict in West Asia and the anticipated El Nino weather pattern could increase inflation pressures in the country. In the same statement, the RBI noted that the Indian economy continues to show resilience despite these external risks. No further details on policy response were provided in the source.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: White House says Melania Trump secured ceasefire in Oleshky
stories.summary: The White House announced that former First Lady Melania Trump helped secure a cease‑fire between Russian and Ukrainian forces in the occupied city of Oleshky. Both sides said they would stop firing at 02:00 GMT on 27 October and work to evacuate residents and allow humanitarian aid. Oleshky has been under Russian control since February 2022, and residents have been facing severe shortages.
stories.why: The pause could enable delivery of food, medicine and water to civilians in a city on the brink of disaster.
stories.previousTitle: White House says Melania Trump secured ceasefire in Oleshky, Ukraine
stories.previousSummary: The White House announced that former First Lady Melania Trump had “successfully secured” a localized cease‑fire between Russian and Ukrainian forces in the occupied city of Oleshky, slated to begin on 29 October. Both sides reportedly agreed to stop firing at 02:00 GMT on 27 October and to allow evacuation of residents and delivery of aid. Oleshky has been under Russian control since February 2022 and residents have faced severe shortages.

stories.title: Deadly shooting near Paris is a 'racist terrorist attack', Macron says
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron has labelled a gun attack in a Parisian suburb which killed one person and injured five others "a racist terrorist attack". The attack unfolded over some 15 minutes with the attacker opening fire from his car - first in Trappes to the south-west of Paris, and then in nearby La Verrière - appearing to target people of migrant origin.

stories.title: Denmark to end mink farming by August 2029 after dropping EU exemption bid
stories.summary: Denmark will cease mink farming by August 2029 after the government decided not to pursue an exemption to the EU‑wide ban on the practice. The ban is scheduled to take effect on 7 August next year, followed by a two‑year transition period to wind down remaining operations. The decision reflects a shrinking fur market, a past Covid‑related outbreak in mink, and animal‑welfare concerns.
stories.why: The policy ends Denmark’s mink‑fur sector, which had been the world’s largest producer, impacting animal welfare and related economic activity.
stories.previousTitle: Denmark to ban mink farming in government U-turn
stories.previousSummary: Mink farming will end in Denmark by August 2029 after the government decided to drop plans to pursue an exemption to an EU-wide ban on the practice. Denmark was once the largest producer of mink fur in the world, but the industry has declined due to global bans on fur farming, a decline in the fur trade and an earlier outbreak of a Covid strain in the nation's mink population.

stories.title: Tata Motors CV posts Rs 2,138 crore Q2 profit
stories.summary: Tata Motors Ltd achieved a standalone net profit of ₹2,138 crore for the September quarter, reversing last year's loss. Consolidated profit also increased to ₹1,257 crore, aided by a drop in mark-to-market losses.
